subject: Bankify pilot: SCC module alignment, controller/processor split & DPA next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bankify.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: Bankify pilot: SCC module alignment, controller/processor split & DPA next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single thread to track items for the pilot procurement/legal intake.

Recap (high level):
- Pilot scope: limited production pilot for Bankify transaction enrichment (anonymized transaction metadata + merchant enrichment).
- Redwood role: processing transaction metadata and returning enrichment vectors/backfill; we do not ingest bank account numbers or full PANs.
- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in scope; we will provide the report once mutual NDA is complete.

GDPR-specific items we discussed:
1) DPA request: Bankify asked for a DPA with explicit clauses around sub-processor notifications, data retention (30 days for raw KV cache; 12 months for aggregated telemetry), and right-to-be-forgotten flows.
2) SCCs: Bankify legal prefers using the modular SCC approach — their counsel suggested Module 2 (processor-to-processor) for some telemetry flows and Module 1 (controller-to-processor) for customer personal data in enrichment. We should confirm mapping and pick the SCC "module profile" that fits the pilot.
3) Controller/processor split: Primary ask is to confirm which party is controller vs processor for purpose of customer PII vs telemetry/ops logs. On the call we agreed Redwood will be processor for enrichment outputs; Bankify will remain controller for underlying account data. We should turn that into an explicit clause in the DPA.

Attachments I’m including for review: Redwood_DPA_Draft_v2.pdf (initial DPA that reflects our standard processor terms) and SCC_options_matrix.xlsx (matrix mapping typical flows to SCC module choices).

Proposed next steps and owners:
- Elena / Bankify legal: share any DPA redlines and confirm which SCC modules your counsel prefers by EOD Tue (2026-11-17). (Action: Bankify legal)
- Redwood (Ben + Hannah): review your redlines, map to our sub-processor list and provide a narrow set of counter-proposals (if any). (Action: Ben)
- Technical: Ben to provide a short note on telemetry retention/what is considered PII vs telemetry. (Action: Ben)
- Security questionnaire: we’ll kick off the vendor security questionnaire (VSQ) — if you have your standard intake URL or template, please share.

If that looks right I’ll loop in our legal ops contact and drop the DPA into your shared Drive link. Happy to join a quick call with your counsel next week if that helps accelerate.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bankify.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
Cc: Bankify Legal <legal@bankify.com>, Bankify Security <security@bankify.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 18:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Bankify pilot: SCC module alignment, controller/processor split & DPA next steps

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear notes, appreciated.

A few clarifications from our side after circulating the internal summary:
- Bankify position on controller/processor: Bankify will remain controller for account and transaction-level data. Redwood will be processor for enrichment outputs. For operational telemetry (API request logs, edge traces) we need to treat some fields as "processor-generated" but Bankify still requires the right to request deletion for traces that reference identifiable customer IDs — we will mark those fields in the VSQ.
- SCC preference: our legal counsel prefers a mixed approach — Module 1 where Bankify is controller, Module 2 for certain cross-processor flows (e.g., when Redwood calls a third-party enrichment partner). Can you confirm whether Redwood uses downstream enrichment partners for the pilot? If so, we need the sub-processor disclosure and a commitment to notify us 30 days before onboarding.
- SOC 2: please send the latest Type II report under NDA. We will share our intake link for the security questionnaire separately.

We attach our DPA request template (Bankify_DPA_Request.docx) with a handful of redline suggestions in the margin — mostly around notification timelines and audit rights.

I’ll aim to get a more formal redline back to you by next Tuesday. Also happy to set a 30 min legal sync early next week; what times work for your counsel?

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Partnerships, Bankify
[Attachment: Bankify_DPA_Request.docx (Word, 48KB)]

Subject: Re: Bankify pilot: SCC module alignment, controller/processor split & DPA next steps

Quick internal note — threading tasks so we don’t drop anything:
- I’ll pull together a short technical appendix that enumerates what we consider PII in the enrichment payload, and how telemetry fields are redacted/hashed by default. Target EOD Monday (2026-11-16).
- I’ll also prepare our current sub-processor list and the standard 30-day notification language for adding sub-processors; will attach to the internal DPA response.
- Laura: can you confirm any precedent around agreeing mixed SCC modules in prior EU pilots? If we need to propose a single canonical approach (easier for legal), I can draft language that maps flows to Module 1 or Module 2 explicitly.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bankify.com>, Bankify Legal <legal@bankify.com>, Bankify Security <security@bankify.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Bankify pilot: SCC module alignment, controller/processor split & DPA next steps

Thanks Elena — appreciate the prompt clarifications and the template. Next actions from Redwood side:
- We uploaded our redline-friendly DPA draft to the shared folder and attached the SCC mapping worksheet that explicitly shows which pilot flows we recommend mapping to Module 1 vs Module 2. See link above and attached copies.
- Ben attached a short technical appendix (see SCC_options_matrix.xlsx tab "PII vs Telemetry") that calls out the fields we treat as PII and the default retention windows.
- Sub-processors: Redwood will not call external enrichment partners for the initial pilot. If that changes we commit to the 30-day notification and will include a right-to-object window for Bankify. We added that language in Section 5.3 of the DPA draft.

Proposed timeline (so legal teams can calendar):
- Tue 2026-11-17: Bankify legal to provide initial redlines / indicate SCC module preference.
- Wed 2026-11-18: Redwood (Ben + legal ops) to send counter-proposal and call out any non-starter items.
- Thu 2026-11-19: 30-min legal alignment call (if needed) — we can host 09:00-11:00 UTC or 14:00-16:00 UTC.

If that works, please confirm the Tue timeline and preferred time window for Thu’s call (if you think one will be required).

Thanks — looking forward to finalizing so we can start the pilot in December.

Hannah
